theme: Spring Capsule Launch — 3 Pieces, Infinite Outfits
previewText: 3 pieces that work with everything you already own
brief:
Launch email for the Spring Into Work campaign. Lead with the capsule concept — position 3 hero pieces (blazer, ponte pant, knit blouse) as the answer to her Monday-morning paralysis. Show styled outfits, not individual products. CTA: Shop the Spring Capsule.

Tone: Practical, warm. She's busy — get to the point. Avoid trend language.
heroImageBrief:
Subject: Woman in her early 40s, business casual, blazer over silk blouse, ponte trousers
Setting: Clean modern office hallway or conference room doorway, natural light through windows
Wardrobe: Anne Klein navy blazer, blush knit top, black ponte pant, low block heel
Mood: Confident, unhurried, competent
Avoid: Posed smiles, casual loft settings, anything that reads 'fashion shoot'
AI image prompt: Professional woman in her 40s wearing a navy blazer and bone-white blouse walking through a bright modern office hallway, natural window light, confident candid expression, editorial style photography
notes: Coordinate with site team to update hero banner same day

theme: How I Wear It: Navy Blazer 3 Ways
brief:
Carousel post showing the Anne Klein navy blazer styled 3 ways for different work scenarios: (1) board meeting — blazer + ponte pant + heel, (2) casual Friday — blazer + dark jeans + flat, (3) client dinner — blazer + dress + statement earring.

Caption angle: 'One blazer. Three weeks of outfits.' Link in bio to shop.
Hashtags: #WorkwearFormula #AnneKlein #PolishedProfessional
heroImageBrief: Three-panel carousel. Each panel: same model, same blazer, completely different look and setting. Clean white or neutral background for consistency across panels. Model should read as the same real professional, not a different model per slide.

previewText: Real outfits for real work days — no styling degree required
brief:
Mid-week engagement email. Feature 2-3 complete outfit pairings from the spring collection — full head-to-toe looks with specific product names and prices. Lean into the 'formula' concept: top + bottom + one accessory = done.

Include a section on fabric care ('machine washable ponte' is a conversion trigger for this persona). CTA: Shop the Look for each outfit.
notes: Test two subject line variants: 'Wednesday solved' vs 'The outfit formula she's been looking for'

brief:
Single product spotlight on the ponte trousers. Lead with the practical truth: machine washable, holds shape after 40 washes, works with everything. Show on a real body in motion — walking, seated in a meeting, standing at a desk. Not a flat lay.

Caption: Lead with a pain point ('Raise your hand if you've ruined dry-clean-only trousers at the worst time.') then transition to the solution.

Homepage hero banner for the Spring Into Work campaign launch. Headline should be in the 'no-brainer workwear' register — direct, practical, confident. Not 'Celebrate Spring' or 'Refresh Your Look.' Something like: 'Spring work wardrobe. Solved.' or 'Three pieces. Every outfit.'

Subhead: 1 sentence speaking to quality and versatility. CTA button: 'Shop the Capsule'.
heroImageBrief: Woman walking purposefully through a bright modern office or lobby, spring light, navy and blush palette, blazer + trousers, no props, no exaggerated pose. She looks like she just made a decision and it was the right one.
notes: Goes live same day as launch email — coordinate timing

theme: Welcome Email Redesign — 15% Off First Order
subjectLine: Welcome to Anne Klein — here's 15% off
previewText: Your first order discount + what to shop first
brief:
Redesigned welcome email to match or beat competitor offers. JNY is at 40% off, WHBM at 20% off, Ann Taylor at 10% off. AK currently offers 15% off first purchase of $125+.

Structure: (1) Warm brand intro — who AK is, what she can expect, (2) 15% off offer clearly displayed with code, (3) 'Start here' product curation — 3-4 bestsellers with images and prices, (4) 'What makes us different' — 1-2 sentences on quality and fit consistency.

Do NOT lead with the discount. Lead with the brand promise, then reveal the offer. Her first impression should be 'this brand gets me' not 'here's a coupon.'
notes: Compare against competitive benchmark in email_analysis.json before finalizing offer amount
